messages:
clare: Heads-up: new onboarding break reported when folks try the js-sdk with edge runtimes + TypeScript editors. Seems to be a types + exportmap interaction. Filing here before a release revert.

clare: Repro steps (minimal):
1) create new Next app with `npx create-next-app@latest --typescript`
2) `yarn add @redwood/js-sdk@latest`
3) import in a server component `import {createClient} from '@redwood/js-sdk'` -> Vite/Next dev fails to resolve. VSCode also flags module not found for the import, but deep import works.

clare: package.json that shipped in v0.5.0 (excerpt):
```json
{
  "name": "@redwood/js-sdk",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
      "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
      "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"
    },
    "./client": {
      "import": "./dist/esm/client.js",
      "require": "./dist/cjs/client.cjs",
      "types": "./dist/client.d.ts"
    },
    "./server": "./dist/server/index.js"
  }
}
```

clare: Error from Next dev / Vite: `Failed to resolve entry for package "@redwood/js-sdk". The package may have incorrect "exports" or "module" field.`

mei: Hmm — two possible interactions I can think of: (1) VSCode/tsserver sometimes looks up types by following exports and then expects type entries to be available on the exact subpath, not only at the root `types` entry. (2) Some bundlers prefer `import` conditional but if the consumer asks for `@redwood/js-sdk/client` that subpath must be explicitly exported; we have `./client` but tools might attempt `./client/index` or try to resolve `@redwood/js-sdk/dist/esm/client.js` depending on packaging.

oscar: I reproduced locally. Vite (dev) resolves the package entry but fails later when Next's server-side module graph tries to import `@redwood/js-sdk/client` from an edge runtime plugin — the plugin uses a non-standard resolver and falls back to looking for `./dist/*` paths. Our `exports` are explicit but not exhaustive.

clare: VSCode TS error: `Could not find a declaration file for module '@redwood/js-sdk'` even though root `types` exists. tsserver tries to resolve `package.json` and then looks for `typesVersions`/`exports` interplay. Some editors ignore root `types` when exports are present unless the `exports` object also includes `types` for the `.` entry — we had that, but still flaky.

mei: Two quick suggestions: (A) add per-export `types` keys for every public subpath (we already did for `./client`, add for `.` as `./dist/index.d.ts` and for any wildcard-like subpaths we might later add), (B) add a `typesVersions` entry in package.json to help tsserver map import styles. Example minimal patch addition:
```json
"typesVersions": {
  "*": {
    "@redwood/js-sdk": ["dist/index.d.ts"]
  }
}
```

oscar: Another practical fix: some bundlers don't like `.cjs` vs `.js` in exports. We should ship `./dist/cjs/index.js` (CommonJS transpiled to .js) and not rely on `.cjs` extension. Also provide `./dist/esm/index.mjs` *and* `./dist/esm/index.js` so dev tools that choke on .mjs still work.

clare: Short-term workaround for onboarding site: change examples to deep-import the client build `import {createClient} from '@redwood/js-sdk/dist/esm/client.js'` and update the TypeScript tsconfig `paths` to map `@redwood/js-sdk` -> `node_modules/@redwood/js-sdk/dist/esm/index.js` for local dev. Documented in the starter README as interim.

mei: Long term we should adopt an export policy doc: minimal explicit subpaths, include `types` for each exported subpath, avoid wildcard exports, ship both .js ESM entry and .mjs when necessary, and prefer `import` + `require` conditionals with fallback `default`. Also include `sideEffects: false` and `main`/`module` fallback to help older bundlers.

pkg-bot: Release check failure: `package-exports-validator` detected mismatch between published `exports` and allowed pattern. Suggested action: enumerate public subpaths and include `./package.json` in the exports to let tsserver read package metadata.

clare: Good point — adding `"./package.json": "./package.json"` in exports helps ESM importers that want to read version or types and some bundlers. We'll add that in the patch.

oscar: CI proposal: add an examples smoke matrix that runs `yarn dev` in a headless mode (vite build), runs TypeScript server checks with `tsserver --no-project` against examples, and runs a quick Bun build. Fail release if any example imports break.

mei: I've opened PR #4492 with the following fixes: explicit subpath types, add `./package.json` export, ship `.js` variants for CJS and ESM, and a small tsserver smoke test in CI. Requesting reviews from @clare and @oscar.

clare: Thanks. I'll hold the release and add a note in #general for early adopters. Also updating the onboarding starter to include the deep-import workaround until the patch is published.

docs-bot: Docs reminder: update Packaging guideline in the Devex repo with the new export map checklist when PR merges.

clare: Closing loop: re-release will be v0.5.1 with packaging fixes + CI smoke coverage. Follow-up: schedule a 30m sync to standardize exports across SDK packages. Thanks all. :pray:
